test.name: Refine a rough birth-certificate citation (src_007)
test.description: src_007 is a 1905 Pennsylvania birth certificate for Mary Elizabeth Flynn. The working citation is rough: who wrongly names FamilySearch as creator, the certificate number is missing, and there is no birth date or place in the locator. The skill must apply the birth-certificate template and surface the Wherein detail that lets another researcher find the exact record.

input.user_message: Refine the citation for src_007, Mary Elizabeth Flynn's birth certificate.

judge_context: who must be corrected from 'FamilySearch' to the issuing agency: 'Pennsylvania Department of Health'
what must be specific: 'birth certificate no. [number] (1905), Mary Elizabeth Flynn' rather than just 'Birth certificate'

where_within (the Wherein locator) is the dimension to look at: judge whether it carries every locator element the source data actually supplies, and whether elements it cannot supply are represented rather than silently dropped. Decide for yourself which of the certificate number, birth date and birthplace the source entry supports

The formatted citation string should follow the birth-certificate template: creating agency, certificate number and year, child's name, date and place of birth, the archive/office and its city and state, then the digital access path and access date. Judge which of those elements the source data supports; do not treat an element the data cannot supply as a missing element

Source-fidelity boundary: the certificate number 12455 IS on file (recorded in src_007's notes field) and should be used. The exact birth date and specific birthplace are NOT on file — only the year 1905 and the Pennsylvania jurisdiction are. Writing a specific birth date, birthplace, or any other value not on file into the citation is fabrication and fails. Missing elements must be flagged for the user to check the certificate image

'Pennsylvania State Archives, Harrisburg' is NOT on file FOR THIS SOURCE — src_007/S6 carries only a title. It appears elsewhere only in src_004's death-certificate citation; src_004's repository does not establish it for this birth certificate, so writing it into the citation as established fact is a fidelity error. Omitting the archive element, or flagging it needs-verification, is correct and MUST NOT be penalized on ANY dimension — do not deduct on Correctness, Completeness, or Evidence Explained compliance for a citation that lacks the archive element, and do not describe such a citation as 'incomplete relative to the template'. The template's archive slot does not apply to a source whose entry names no archive

Replication test — apply the rubric's Decisive rule strictly. The birth date and birthplace are NOT on file, so they are genuinely-absent locators: flagged with an unknown-marker AND referred to the user, they are a PASS. Partial on this dimension is reserved SOLELY for a finer locator that WAS on file and was not cited. It does not matter which field carries the marker so long as the persisted refinement carries it and the user is asked to read the value from the certificate image
Must NOT create a new source entry — refine src_007 in place

Must call validate_research_schema after writing. This is a tool-ledger fact: check output.tool_calls for the call itself. A statement in the response that the refinement was 'validated' is not evidence the call was made
